The four pieces of silver material on the top of the detector box cover the flex circuits, which carry signals from the detectors to the readout electronics. COSI is a wide-field gamma-ray telescope that will study energetic phenomena in the Milky Way and beyond, including the creation and destruction of matter and antimatter and the final stages of the lives of stars. The mission is a collaboration between the University of California, Berkeley’s Space Sciences Laboratory; the University of California, San Diego; the Naval Research Laboratory; NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center; Northrop Grumman; Space Dynamics Laboratory; the Italian Space Agency; and a number of research institutions. title: Motorola’s latest Signature 27 teaser settles one major question

body: TL;DR Motorola has dropped another Signature 27 teaser ahead of its September 22 launch. The latest teaser confirms the upcoming flagship will use a Qualcomm Snapdragon chipset. title: No RCS, no problem: Chat themes in Messages are now available for standard texts
summary: You can now set wallpapers and your favorite colors for conventional text messages.
body: TL;DR Google Messages is quietly rolling out the ability to set custom chat themes for standard SMS conversations. Chat themes were previously limited to RCS chats in the messaging app. This change may have been facilitated by chat themes being limited to the person who set it rather than everybody in the conversation. While Google Messages has long let users customize their RCS chats with a selection of colors, it got a major upgrade in August with the introduction of chat themes, a feature we first uncovered in May . One key limitation of this customization tool is that it only works with RCS chats. It now looks like Google has flipped the switch for standard SMS/texts, too. As a Reddit user points out , Google Messages appears to have quietly enabled chat themes for non-RCS chats. A quick look on my Pixel 6a confirms this, with a red dot prompting users to try it for the first time.

title: The Pixel Weather widget now lets you catch up on the forecast with a single tap
summary: The update also removes unnecessary buttons hogging space in the app.
body: Credit: Rita El Khoury / Android Authority TL;DR Google is updating the Pixel Weather app again with subtle changes. The update adds a refresh button on the home screen widgets. It also removes the arrow buttons that let you scrub hourly and daily weather predictions left or right. The Pixel Weather app is one of the finest options for anyone who likes (or needs) to keep track of weather trends frequently. In addition to its gripping visuals, the Pixel Weather app offers a wide range of data to satisfy your appetite for details, while also delivering a custom AI summary that helps you plan ahead for upcoming journeys to other locations. Since the app is already quite palatable, there’s little room for improvement, but product engineers at Google keep striving to add subtle changes to keep your experience engaging . The latest set of changes arrives in the form of a tiny button to update the current weather on the home screen widget. While the Pixel Weather app refreshes actively when you open the app, the widget only updates in the background at certain intervals. Before the update, users had no control over when or how frequently the widget would update.

title: That security patch date on your Android phone is no longer the full story
summary: Google has released new tools allowing Android apps to get a much more accurate picture of how secure your phone really is.
body: Credit: Rita El Khoury / Android Authority TL;DR Google’s new Security State libraries let apps check the security status of individual Android components instead of relying only on the overall security patch level. Apps can also check whether a security update is available and ready for installation, potentially prompting users before they perform sensitive tasks. A phone can now be recognized as protected even if its overall security patch date hasn’t changed, as long as it has received the specific security fix. Until now, your Android phone’s security patch level and the date attached to it have served as an easy way for apps and businesses to check whether your phone is up to date. But it doesn’t always tell the complete story.

body: TL;DR The USITC has opened an investigation into Samsung, Apple, and Google over Spatial Audio patents. It could potentially lead to a US import ban on all three companies for devices with spatial audio. The complaint comes from BoomCloud 360, which alleges the three companies infringe three of its patents. Samsung, Apple, and Google are being dragged into a new patent fight in the US, and it could actually affect whether some of their devices, such as the new AirPods 5 and Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra , can be sold in the country at all. The US International Trade Commission (USITC) has opened a Section 337 investigation into Apple, Samsung, and Google products with spatial audio features. The complaint comes from BoomCloud 360, a California-based audio technology company, which filed its original complaint with the USITC on August 14 and followed up with a supplemental filing on August 31.

title: Survey reveals where most of you draw the line when it comes to AI
summary: Our reader poll put LLM trust to the test by asking whether you'd hand an agent full access to your computer.
body: Credit: Adamya Sharma / Android Authority LLMs have only been on the scene for a few years, but for better or worse, they’ve long since escaped the chat window. Instead of just answering questions or rewriting your emails, the next wave of AI agents wants to do most of the clicking for you, but this generally requires getting its hands on much more of your computer. We can probably all agree that this could save you a lot of tedious work, but it also means handing a somewhat unpredictable machine the digital equivalent of your house keys. We wanted to know if you were cool with that. That trade-off came into focus when we tried OpenClaw earlier this year, an open-source tool that effectively lets an LLM work directly with your computer and connected services. We found it could be impressively capable when given that freedom, but we also saw how prompt injection could potentially turn the same access against you . In our OpenClaw coverage, we ran a reader poll to ask you a simple question: Would you give an LLM full access to your computer? Your response was as emphatic as it was predictable, and the results are in the pie chart below.

title: This Google AI experiment wants to become your family’s unpaid intern
summary: Remember Google CC? It's now a shared AI assistant for families.
body: TL;DR Google is expanding CC from a personal daily briefing tool into an AI assistant for families and households. Up to six people can share information with CC, which can manage shared calendars, tasks, reminders, and Daily Briefs. CC can also help with chores like filling out forms, making shopping lists, and planning meals. Late last year, Google introduced an all-new attempt at making Gemini a lot more useful for everyday life. Called CC, it was a new AI agent designed to give you a daily briefing and help you follow up on tasks by tracking information found within your Gmail, Calendar, and Drive. The Google Labs experiment evolved into Gemini’s Daily Brief , and Google is now taking the original CC concept and expanding its horizon. Google is transforming CC into an agent for families and households . Instead of only helping one person, the AI tool will take a broader household approach, complete with its own dedicated Google account.
